title: Mary Anning: Stone and Light
dek: The fossil hunter who survived lightning and taught science to read deep time.
mortality_event: Survived a lightning strike as an infant, then spent a short life uncovering extinct worlds from the Lyme Regis cliffs before dying of breast cancer at 47.
citation_passage: Mary Anning (1799–1847) was a fossil collector and pioneering paleontologist from Lyme Regis on England's Jurassic Coast. She learned to find and prepare fossils with her father and developed her knowledge of geology and anatomy through study. After her brother Joseph found an ichthyosaur skull, she excavated the rest of its skeleton. Her later discoveries included a complete plesiosaur skeleton and a pterosaur. Scientists studied and purchased her finds, but often failed to credit her contribution, and the Geological Society did not admit women. She died of breast cancer aged forty-seven. This eight-page biographical comic follows a short life whose patient work helped reveal extinct forms of life.
